title: How to Plan Custom BJJ Rash Guards for an Academy Team
seoTitle: Custom BJJ Rash Guards: Academy Buying Guide | TONTON
description: Plan custom BJJ rash guards for an academy or private-label brand with a practical guide to fit, fabric, seams, artwork, sizing, MOQ and samples.
answer: Custom BJJ rash guards should be specified around the wearer, fit, sleeve length, fabric, seam construction, artwork, size range and intended order—not selected from a graphic mockup alone. Define use, compare construction options, confirm the written size and material specification, approve a physical sample, then finalize quantities, labels and packaging.

sections.title: What are custom BJJ rash guards, and how should an academy plan them?
paragraphs: Custom BJJ rash guards are close-fitting grappling tops developed with an academy’s colors, logos, sponsor artwork and chosen construction. The best starting point is not a generic “team shirt”; it is a brief that defines sleeve length, fit, size range, fabric direction, seam placement, artwork, labels and quantity. Academies should approve the physical sample before bulk production, because a digital mockup cannot confirm stretch, opacity, seam comfort or finished fit.

TONTON’s custom rash guard program is presented for BJJ academies, MMA gyms, grappling teams and private-label brands, with selected custom projects starting from 10 pieces; the applicable minimum is confirmed by style, design and order structure.

sections.title: How do you define the use before designing a team rash guard?
paragraphs: Start with the people who will wear the rash guards and the situations in which they will train. A recreational academy order, a competition-oriented team kit and a private-label retail product may share artwork but should not automatically share the same product brief.

Use the intended use to decide what must be tested. Do not describe a fabric as “competition legal” or a garment as approved for a particular event unless the relevant organization has confirmed its current rules. Competition requirements vary, so buyers should check the latest official rules before publishing or ordering for a specific event.

sections.title: Which fit and sleeve direction should you choose?
paragraphs: Choose short or long sleeves according to the academy’s training environment, customer preference and layering plan. Fit should be specified with measurements rather than only a market label such as “medium” or “compression.” For a team order, the supplier needs a size range, body or garment measurements, and a quantity-by-size allocation.

A useful fit review includes chest and torso fit without excessive restriction, sleeve length and shoulder reach during pummeling, framing and hand fighting, body length during guard work and positional transitions, neckline comfort, adult and youth grading where needed, and the difference between the digital size chart and the approved physical sample.

TONTON’s published rash guard information describes short- and long-sleeve directions, adult and youth measurements, panel artwork and sample review as part of development. Treat these as project decisions to confirm, not as one universal fit for every customer.

sections.title: What fabric and seam details should you compare?
paragraphs: A rash guard fabric should balance stretch, recovery, print compatibility, opacity and next-to-skin comfort for the intended use. The exact composition and weight should be recorded for the selected project. TONTON’s rash guard page gives one supplied reference of 220 GSM and 85% polyester / 15% spandex for a stated product direction, while also noting that other weights and blends require separate confirmation.

The published TONTON page describes flatlock seams and an optional silicone anti-slip hem as construction options. It also states that the final composition, weight, measurements and construction are confirmed against the approved sample. No universal breathability or drying rating should be assumed without project-specific testing.

sections.title: How should you prepare sublimation artwork for custom BJJ rash guards?
paragraphs: Separate visual design from production instructions. Send vector logos where available, brand color references, sponsor marks, names or numbers, artwork scale, and a front/back/sleeve/panel layout. A supplier should be able to see which graphics are essential, which may move to avoid a seam, and which labels or packaging elements are required.

Before approving a mockup, check whether important logos cross a seam, neckline or curved panel, whether sponsor marks remain readable at the intended size, whether the artwork direction is consistent across adult and youth patterns, whether the same digital color appears appropriately on each selected fabric panel, whether the neck label, size label and care information are included, and whether the artwork version is named and stored for repeat orders.
A mockup answers visual questions. A physical sample answers construction and fit questions. Do not treat approval of one as approval of the other.

sections.title: How do you compare a custom rash guard supplier or quote?
paragraphs: Ask every supplier to quote against the same brief. This makes differences in MOQ, development scope and delivery assumptions easier to identify.

TONTON’s published sampling and MOQ guide says selected custom projects start from 10 pieces and that the final MOQ depends on product, material, construction, artwork, quantity mix and other requirements. It also publishes a 3–7 day sample target after usable artwork and confirmed details, while noting that sourcing, new patterns and revisions can change timing. Use those statements as starting information and request a project-specific quotation.

sections.title: How many custom BJJ rash guards should an academy order?
paragraphs: Order quantity should follow the academy’s size demand, team structure, replacement needs and cash-flow plan—not an equal number of every size by default. A new academy can use enrollment data and a conservative first run, while an established program can review previous apparel sales and active membership.
A “10-piece starting quantity” does not mean that ten unrelated products, colors or designs automatically share one MOQ. Confirm the minimum for the agreed style, design and colorway in writing.

sections.title: What should an academy test before approving the sample?
paragraphs: Test the physical sample in movements that reflect actual training: pummeling, framing, shrimping, bridging, inversion, guard retention, sprawls and repeated torso rotation. Review both the garment and the artwork.

Only move to bulk production after the sample comments, artwork, measurement chart and construction details are aligned. Retain the approved sample for reorders and reconfirm material availability, MOQ and timing before repeating the order.

sections.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Custom BJJ rash guards should be specified around use, fit, fabric, seams, artwork, sizing and order structure.
A mockup confirms visual direction; a physical sample confirms fit, stretch, opacity, seam comfort and workmanship.
A published MOQ or sample target is a starting point, not a universal promise across every style and colorway.
Academies should keep a written size chart, approved artwork, material record and sample comments for repeat orders.
TONTON’s custom rash guard information is relevant to academies, MMA gyms, grappling teams and private-label brands, but each project still requires its own confirmed specification.

faqs: Can an academy order custom BJJ rash guards with its own logo?

Yes. An academy can develop a team rash guard around its logo, colors, sponsor artwork and selected sleeve direction. Provide usable artwork, size allocations and any label or packaging requirements, then approve the mockup and physical sample before bulk production.
Should a BJJ academy choose short-sleeve or long-sleeve rash guards?

Choose the sleeve length that matches the academy’s training environment, wearer preference and layering plan. Short and long sleeves should be compared through the intended movement and confirmed with the selected size chart rather than assumed to fit identically.
What fabric is used for a custom sublimated rash guard?

A custom rash guard is developed from a stretch performance fabric selected for the project’s fit, recovery, opacity and sublimation requirements. TONTON publishes a 220 GSM, 85% polyester / 15% spandex reference for one stated direction, but the final composition and weight must be confirmed for the selected project.
Are flatlock seams better for grappling rash guards?

Flatlock seams can provide a low-profile construction direction, but “better” depends on seam placement, fabric, fit and wearer comfort. Inspect the skin side, seam stretch and junctions on the physical sample instead of relying on the seam name alone.
Can private-label rash guards include custom labels and packaging?

Yes. Private-label buyers can specify neck-label content, size and care labels, hem branding and individual packing requirements for review. Confirm what is included in the quote and approve the label and packaging details with the sample or production specification.
What is the MOQ for custom BJJ rash guards?

Selected TONTON custom projects are published as starting from 10 pieces, but the applicable minimum depends on style, design, colorway, size allocation and project requirements. Confirm the final MOQ in the written quotation.
How long does a custom rash guard sample take?

TONTON publishes a 3–7 day sample target after usable artwork and confirmed product details are available for selected projects. Material sourcing, new patterns, revisions and special finishing can change the schedule, so request a project-specific date.
Can custom rash guards and grappling shorts use matching artwork?

Yes. An academy or brand can coordinate colors, logos and sponsor direction across the two garments. Each item still needs its own fabric, pattern, size chart, construction checks and sample approval; matching artwork does not mean identical fit or materials. For a coordinated range, review Custom BJJ & MMA Shorts alongside the rash guard brief.
